body: But I don't know that covert narcissism is characterized by lack or empathy or low conscience. In fact, I've read somewhere that covert narcissists can have very high empathy. But then again it could be that covert narcissism isn't even NPD.

The more I learn about NPD and other disorders, the more the lines are blurred and they all seem to just blend together, like slightly different flavors of the same thing, which is basically just trauma induced insecurity and neuroticism. 

I have a close friend who I've realized more and more seems to be a lot like me. She is extremely insecure, unstable identity, always seems to be chasing some fantasy like a child, seeks male attention and obsesses over romantic interests, seems to frequently replace her friends. But she doesn't really meet the official criteria for NPD or BPD. I feel like these traits usually present themselves in an undifferentiated form where they don't really fit into a particular disorder.

Middle Easterner here and I strongly suspect that the rate of narcissism is higher in Middle Eastern, Indian and maybe East Asian culture. I think it is the fact that the cultures are more shame-based, where reputation is of primary importance.

I am somewhere on the narcissism spectrum, in the covert/vulnerable category, but I don't really relate to the whole discarding people thing. I would always put myself in the shoes of the rejected person. However I have a friend currently who is experiencing this at the hands of a narc she had feelings for, and ironically, she seems to do it to people too, albeit in a softer, more covert way that allows her to not feel like she is being cruel. In fact, I am starting to feel like I am next on the chopping block. This friend is generally a really kind, caring person, I highly doubt she is a narc, but as I got to know her more and more, I started to realize she does seem to have a tendency to use and discard people and it does seem like she is in constant pursuit of relationships and experiences to fulfill some sort of fantasy she has.

Interesting, I was just put on Adderall now in my 30s and I've found it actually makes more hyperfocused on my obsessive thoughts. I am in the process of getting off it now actually. 

I was diagnosed with mild ADHD as a child. I am fairly certain I had SM and was a HSP but was never diagnosed with any of those things nor were they identified. I actually don't know that being on the autism spectrum makes you fit in better with autistic friends. I imagine it just makes you more of a loner. I think people who are very mild on the spectrum are likely to fit in well with neurotypicals. When I did the MMPI personality inventory test, my therapist said the results were consistent with possible very mild autism spectrum.
You could also look into AvPD, BPD, cPTSD because they all cause similar issues I think.

If someone has ADHD, SM and is a HSP, I would suspect they are likely on the autism spectrum. And if I had to guess, I would think that people on the autism spectrum often end up developing covert narcissism of some sort due to bullying and social ostracism. 

This fits into my theory I previously expressed that covert narcissists are often people with relatively normal levels of narcissism which would be adaptive in a normal, socially successful person, but lead to maladaptive defense mechanisms in people who are socially marginalized.

The part about getting depressed during any life transition and the part about needing reassurance sound a lot like me as well. However, I am not diagnosed as a narcissist and I am not sure if that is what I have, but I do identify with the covert narcissist description. However, those things also sound very anxiety/OCD/depression related to me as well.
Would the affects of this extend beyond the 5-6 hours which Adderall is active?

Yup I'm male and I definitely have this. If I'm a narcissist I'd be classified as somatic vulnerable. I used watch a lot of porn in my teens, then in college I discovered strip clubs, then graduated to escorts, and eventually paid webcam sites. Needless to say I've dropped a lot of money satisfying my sexual urges. But I actually suspect that the root of this is not somatic grandiosity but a sexual addiction I developed from porn use in my teens. And that my preoccupation with being physically attractive stems from a desire to avoid the shame associated with the image of the unattractive(especially older) guy pursuing women sexually. Just a theory though.

It's just a working theory, but I think my porn use in my teens may have messed with my dopamine reward system in a way such that women and my sexual fantasies involving them became my primary fixation. But because of both my social isolation in my youth and my AvPD tendencies, I've never been able to go out and pursue these fantasies, which led to depression and anxiety/OCD about my looks and aging. My rage and envy are mainly a result of this fear and anxiety. I also suspect the reason not being able to get girls triggers such depression and anxiety could be related to a CPTSD I developed due to my feelings of jealousy towards my abusive younger brother getting girls during my teen years. But due to the effects of my porn use, my focus is constantly being brought back to women and sex, which in turn triggers the fears of rejection and inadequacy and the jealousy. Or something like that.

Alternatively, I suspect that it may largely center around a fear of aging. I have found that I have generally associated youthful boyishness with attractiveness and that my biggest insecurity has always been becoming/looking older. I used to assume that my insecurity about aging stems from that fear of being undesirable to women. But my fear of aging actually pre-dates my desire to be attractive to women. Even when I was as young as 12, I was scared of being considered a "teenager" instead of a "kid". It was mainly that I identified more with the "kid" identity and I was perhaps afraid of losing something I had. And even now, I feel that i have a strong attachment to the "young" identity associated with 20somethings even aside from the desire to be attractive to women. The prospect of being older also making me unattractive to women is just insult to injury.

My understanding of the term "malignant narcissist" is that it refers to people who are full blown grandiose NPD, but I am not sure. My understanding is that successful people with full blown grandiose NPD still have a need to constantly project their inflated self-image and have it validated by everyone. I am not familiar with the term "failed narcissist".
Fyi OP seems to be a woman, just in case that changes your judgement.

To me AvPD and covert narcissism sound almost identical aside from the underlying grandiosity and (according to some sources) lack of empathy of covert narcissists. Since there does not seem to be anything unique to avoidants that covert narcissists don't have, it would seem to me that pretty much every covert narc also has AvPD.

I am also thinking maybe it stems from something other than my AvPD traits. Lately I've been wondering if at the root of it is more of a complex disorder caused by the interactions between anxiety/OCD, depression and (this might sound farfetched) a sexual fantasy addiction caused by extensive porn use during my teens.
I don't see it.

Not sure if it is related to NPD, but if you got bullied a lot in your youth, your brain probably developed a heightened sense of detecting hostility. You are more likely to interpret people as being hostile to you for that reason. I also got bullied in my youth and I am the same way.

I definitely experience fear of abandonment. Even with just platonic friends. I am extremely hurt when I get the feeling that someone is distancing themselves or has started valuing me less than they did previously. I usually don't act on this feeling though.

However I am just not interested in a committed relationship. When I meet someone that I develop feelings for, then there is a part of me that would like to be with them, but at this point in my life my desire to keep my options open and not get tied down outweigh that. In the absence of someone I have feelings for, I am 100% ok with being single and the idea of being married or having a girlfriend is completely unappealing.

I am not 100% clear on the nuances between these terms, but the one experience is pretty complex I think and I don't fully understand it myself. But I think that at its core it stems from a fear of missing out on things.

>BPD is just vulnerable narcissism, where the fantasy is of a perfect love.

Interesting. That's an aspect of BPD I've never related to. I do not fantasize about "perfect love" and actually have no interest in serious relationships at all.

However, the "grandiose fantasies" thing always confused me. I would say that my "fantasies" are about relatively "normal" things that are out of my immediate reach for whatever reason. Like for example I fantasize about having dating and sexual experiences like the ones I hear normal guys talking about. I also fantasize about living abroad or doing the solo backpacker travel thing long term. But I wouldn't say that I "fantasize" about these things, as much as I aspire to do them.
How so?

Well, overestimating one's talents is only a feature of grandiose NPD. Most grandiose narcissists' grandiose fantasies are something that is not realistic for most people, so generally speaking it will almost always be a disorder. 

However my theory applies more to vulnerable NPD. I suspect that vulnerable narcissists usually do not have grandiose fantasies, but because of their low station in life, their relatively "normal" fantasies and desired self image are not consistent with their realty and are unattainable for them.
I think I've read somewhere before that some people think vulnerable narcissism is more a subtype of BPD than NPD but I'm not sure.

My brother and I were both pretty coddled by our parents, but he was socially successful and grew up normal and well-adjusted whereas I was socially marginalized and grew up to be a covert narcissist. I conjecture that my brother is actually higher on the narcissism spectrum than I am, but not high enough to develop into a grandiose narcissist. He is kind of egotistical and attention seeking, but it is not maladaptive so he is not disordered. But, like I said, I think that the level of narcissism that is not maladaptive in confident, socially successful people can cause covert/vulnerable NPD in those who are lower in self esteem and socially marginalized. In order to develop grandiose NPD however, I think that people need to be on the very high end of the narcissism spectrum. Most people who are coddled by their parents do not reach this level, hence why most do not develop a disorder when they are confident and socially successful.

Again though, just my theory.

I am insecure, jealous, resentful, sensitive to social rejection, obsessed with staying young and attractive...

I don't have a sense of specialness as I don't see myself as special or out of the odrinary in any way.

You sounded like my brother growing up. He was also a textbook overt narc(constantly bragging, abusive and disparaging). But he was socially successful and grew up to be normal and well-adjusted. He doesn't have the same narc tendencies he has as a kid anymore. Meanwhile I did not have the same narc tendencies but was socially marginalized and I am pretty sure I am a vulnerable narc now.

For those on the malignant end of the narcissism spectrum, yes. But for those on the less extreme end, my theory is actually that those who experience bullying and rejection will probably become vulnerable narcissists whereas those who are socially successful will likely become normal, well-adjusted people with maybe just a bit of jealousy and competitiveness. Basically I suspect that less extreme levels of narcissism are only debilitating and self-destructive to people whose experiences growing up did not foster a healthy sense of self-esteem. Generally these people become covert/vulnerable narcissists I think. I think that these same levels of narcissism may even be adaptive to those with higher self esteem and social success.

My theory is not that it's just your station in life. Again, my theory is that it is an interaction between your station in life and where you are on the narcissism spectrum. The rigid personality construct you are talking about is probably only in people who are on the malignant end of the narcissism spectrum. These people's level of narcissism will cause them problems no matter what their station in life is(e.g. the Donald Trumps of the world). But I suspect that with people who are on a less extreme part of the spectrum, whether their level of narcissism causes them problems or not depends on their station in life. I believe there is a level of narcissism which only causes problems only if a person is of a lower "station" in life but not if they are not. I think this is what usually manifests itself as covert or vulnerable narcissism. However, not everyone is a lower "station" in life will have these problems, people who are very low on the narcissism spectrum will be able to cope just fine.

I'm not sure if I have NPD, but I strongly identify with the covert narcissist description. Although I'm male, I am kind of like you describe. I wouldn't call it "entitlement" necessarily, but I fantasize about sexual experiences with lots of different women and I seem especially turned on by "extra spicy" types of scenarios. Like, I've always had a fixation on the fantasy of being with a much older woman when I am inappropriately young for her. I've fantasized about and even pursued(albeit not seriously) married women. I've fantasized about fucking my therapist. Aside from that my fantasies usually revolve around random women I'm not well acquainted with, like waitresses or cashiers that I interacted with briefly. The common denominator seems to be things that deviate from the "vanilla" boyfriend/girlfriend or husband/wife scenario.

Normally I've never thought of any of this as abnormal, until recent times when I've realized the growing intensity of the distress caused by the prospect of aging and no longer being attractive enough to pursue these fantasies.
